about: English source text for the 百草衡 / Baicao Heng iOS app. Translate every entry. Keep {0}, {1}… placeholders, **bold** markers, numbers, units (g, ml, mg, kg, °C, %) and Latin / pinyin names in parentheses unchanged; you may reorder placeholders.
ui_strings: No weight-based compounds in this formula (cinnamon, green tea, licorice); below 50 kg dose alerts are tightened
cold in nature; prolonged use damages spleen–stomach yang
Sugar dissolved from brown sugar, rock sugar, honey, longan and jujube; WHO suggests free sugars ideally < 25 g/day
many rich, cloying tonics; prolonged use burdens digestion
Chicken gizzard lining works better swallowed as powder (1.5–3 g per dose); its enzymes do not survive boiling.
Do not boil honey or add it to boiling water. Stir it in once the liquid is below 60 °C to keep its enzymes and limit HMF formation.
Rich, cloying tonics dominate and may cause bloating and poor appetite. Add 3–6 g tangerine peel or 3 g amomum to keep things moving.
Cold and hot herbs are used together and temper each other. If this is not intentional, their effects may cancel out.
Combination, doses and preparation are all within normal ranges.
This formula has a clear bias and is not for long-term use.
A balanced constitution has no marked tendency. Wellness drinks should be mild, low-dose and varied rather than one formula long-term.
Pungent flavor is high; its dispersing action can deplete yin fluids.
Many cloying tonics; they can breed dampness and block qi.
Qi-moving herbs dominate; long-term use can drain qi.
Many astringent herbs, which do not help blood flow.
With allergies, start with a small test amount, especially with flowers such as chrysanthemum and honeysuckle.
Drink warm about 1 hour before meals; tonics absorb better on an empty stomach
Drink warm after meals, or sip through the day like tea
Re-steep 1–2 times until the taste fades; finish within the day.
Re-steep 2–3 times until the taste fades; finish within the day.
One batch per day. Re-boil the dregs once (about 20 minutes), combine both liquids, and drink in two portions, morning and evening.
People with a weak, cold digestion, who feel cold or have loose stools

At the start of a cold or with an acute excess condition

No specific contraindication, but pause during colds, fevers or acute illness
The Five Phases are fairly balanced; the formula is gentle and suited to everyday maintenance.
more blood-nourishing, less of the “qi generates blood” intent
Western herb: doses follow German Commission E / EMA monographs; the nature, flavor and meridian entries are reference attributions from integrative literature (Holmes, Ross), not pharmacopoeial.
Used in both traditions: nature and meridians per the Chinese Pharmacopoeia; Western use per Commission E.

An educational model based on Chinese Pharmacopoeia dose ranges, German Commission E / EMA monographs and TCM materia medica theory. It does not replace diagnosis by a qualified practitioner. With a chronic condition, current medication, pregnancy, or for children, consult a physician or pharmacist first.

Nature is scored Cold −2, Cool −1.2, Slightly cold −1, Neutral 0, Slightly warm +1, Warm +1.5, Hot +2, Very hot +3. Extraction rate is the share of active constituents transferred to the liquid in one pass; solid–liquid equilibrium caps it at about 30–55% for a proper first decoction and 50–70% after a second boil. Potency = grams ÷ usual-dose midpoint × (this extraction ÷ standard-preparation extraction). Five-Phase shares combine the five flavors (sour→Wood, bitter→Fire, sweet→Earth, pungent→Metal, salty→Water) and the meridian organs, half each.
